A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BALD study and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F. Content can be reliably matched despite layout changes.

before.justification: v2 reports original driving and robotics experiments, component ablations, defense evaluations, and annotation comparisons in Section 4 and Appendices A–C.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the benchmark comparisons, ablations, defense experiments, and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The BALD-word, BALD-scene, and BALD-RAG procedures and components remain unchanged in Sections 3.2–3.4. Appendix E retains the same prompt examples.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same driving and household robotics coverage using HighwayEnv, nuScenes/CARLA, and VirtualHome, with the same target and boundary scenarios.

E2.justification: Tables 2–3 retain the original-model, benign-fine-tuning, and BadChain comparisons. The ONION evaluation in Table 5 and fine-tuning defenses in Appendix B also retain the same comparator membership.

E3.justification: The model configurations, metrics, dataset splits, and training settings in Section 4.1 and Appendices A and F are unchanged. Both versions already disclose the separate 19-sample BALD-scene VirtualHome evaluation versus ten tasks for other models.

E4.justification: The component ablations in Table 4, ratio sensitivity and defense analyses in Figure 7, and additional defense and reasoning studies in Appendices B–C are retained without substantive revision. Appendix A.2 retains the same annotation-quality analysis.

E5.justification: Table 3 reports the same three-run robotics evaluation and identical ± values in both versions. No repeated-run, seed, uncertainty-reporting, or statistical-testing changes were found.

E6.justification: Tables 2–5 and 7–8 and Figure 7 retain identical results. For example, Table 2 reports GPT-3.5 BALD-word HighwayEnv ASR of 100.0% and benign accuracy of 99.2% in both versions. Appendix C retains the same qualitative examples.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 retains the same threat-model assumptions and objectives O.1–O.3. No mathematical definitions, derivations, propositions, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about BALD's novelty, three attack mechanisms, effectiveness, stealthiness, and security implications. The added code-availability statement does not redefine the scientific contribution.

C2.justification: The interpretations of attack effectiveness, retrieval dependence, stealthiness, and defense performance remain unchanged. Appendices A.3 and D retain the same qualifications about noncomparable robotics scores, limited evaluation data, and applicability.

D1.justification: v3 adds a linked 'Code is available' statement in the abstract pointing to the BALD project repository; v2 lacks this project-code access information. Existing dataset, prompt, and fine-tuning details remain unchanged. Repository contents cannot be established from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v3 adds Wang et al. (2023d), Zhu et al. (2021), and Zhu et al. (2020) to the introduction's background on autonomous-system safety and uncertainty. These are limited citation additions; BALD's positioning relative to prior attack research remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized grammar and spelling corrections, shortens some phrases, converts the related-work subsection headings into inline headings, updates an author affiliation, and adds acknowledgements. The scientific narrative and section sequence remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds conference headers, resizes Figure 3, moves Figure 5 from page 7 to page 6, and reflows tables, appendix illustrations, and prompt boxes. All figures and tables are retained with unchanged substantive content.

improvement.justification: The new project-code link provides a useful access route, while localized language corrections and additional background citations modestly improve usability and context. The scientific evidence and limitations remain unchanged, and the PDFs do not establish the linked code's completeness or usability.
